---
title: "Exercise 5 — Meta-regression and effect modification"
format: html
---

## Aim

Fit prespecified moderators, interpret coefficients, and distinguish an across-study association from a causal effect.

## 1. Prepare the data

Use the `es` object from the previous exercises, or recreate it from `soil_carbon.csv`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
levels(factor(es$climate))
range(es$duration)
```

Before fitting a model, write down a biological reason why **duration** might modify the reduced-tillage effect on soil carbon.

## 2. Continuous moderator

```{r}
#| eval: false
m_duration <- rma.mv(
  yi, vi,
  mods = ~ ___,
  random = ~ 1 | study_id/effect_id,
  data = es
)
summary(m_duration)
```

1. What does the duration coefficient represent on the lnRR scale?
2. Calculate `exp(coef(m_duration)["duration"])`. What does this represent?
3. Is the coefficient estimated precisely?

## 3. Categorical moderator

```{r}
#| eval: false
es$climate <- factor(es$climate)
levels(es$climate)

m_climate <- rma.mv(
  yi, vi,
  mods = ~ climate,
  random = ~ 1 | study_id/effect_id,
  data = es
)
summary(m_climate)
```

Identify the reference category and explain one climate coefficient without calling it a separate “effect”.

## 4. Two moderators

```{r}
#| eval: false
m_both <- rma.mv(
  yi, vi,
  mods = ~ duration + climate,
  random = ~ 1 | study_id/effect_id,
  data = es
)
summary(m_both)
```

Compare the duration coefficient with the single-moderator model. Why might it change?

## 5. Causal interpretation challenge

A colleague writes:

> “Longer implementation causes reduced tillage to increase soil carbon more strongly.”

Rewrite this claim so that it is supported by an ordinary study-level meta-regression.

Then list **two plausible confounders** of the across-study duration–effect association.

## 6. Extrapolation

The observed durations are limited to the range in the dataset. Would you use this model to predict an effect at 30 years? Explain why or why not.

## 7. Reporting

Write a short results paragraph that includes:

- the moderator being examined and why;
- the estimated direction/magnitude and uncertainty;
- residual heterogeneity;
- a caution about across-study interpretation.

Do not report only the moderator p-value.
